newsitem.title: USA: Bear Stearns seen resigning as adviser to LIPA.
newsitem.headline: Bear Stearns seen resigning as adviser to LIPA.

text.p: Bear Stearns Cos Inc is expected to resign its position as financial adviser to the Long Island Power Authority and will seek a slot on the agency's underwriting syndicate, sources with knowledge of the moves said Tuesday.

The agency is at the center of a proposal to issue as much as $7.3 billion of tax-exempt debt to take over the operations of Long Island Lighting Co. The sources said Bear Stearns would resign this summer, when a new adviser would be selected.

According to one source familiar with the moves, Bear Stearns will continue as adviser to the authority until after the New York State Public Facilities Control Board approves the bond sale needed for a takeover of LILCO.
Officials at Bear Stearns and LIPA were not immediately available for comment.

When Bear Stearns was appointed financial adviser, the agreement gave the firm permission to resign as adviser and compete for underwriting positions when bond sales were contemplated, according to a source familiar with the deal.
Underwriting revenue bonds is considered a more lucrative position than providing financial advisory services.
The agency plans to send out requests for proposals for a new financial adviser in July. One of the criteria for the new adviser is that they do not have a bond underwriting operation.

Some of the contenders for the slot are expected to be Public Financial Management, Public Resources Advisory Group, and O'Brien Partners Inc. The three all have experience advising on New York bond deals and none have underwriting desks.
When a new adviser is selected, Bear Stearns is expected to turn over all information relating to the proposed LILCO takeover to the new adviser, according to the sources.
An underwriting team for the bond deal would be selected in early 1998, if the plan is approved by the Public Facilities Control Board.
